Step 1. Recognize Babylonian positional notation

• Babylonian (or “sexagesimal”) numerals are written in positional notation with “digits” (values 0–59) separated into “places” that represent increasing powers of 60. In a typical “two‐digit” numeral the left group is the 60’s digit and the right group is the units digit. Thus the overall (base‑10) value is:
